turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Onto the scale, please. Readings first, then the doctor.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning. Yes, certainly.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure one sixteen over seventy. Uh, the cuff slipped. Retake is one oh nine over seventy-seven.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Your last pressure was one-forty over eighty-eight, back in March.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Pulse ninety-two. No, sorry, I miscounted. Pulse is seventy-eight, regular.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Weight today sixty-four point five kilos. Last time in March you were sixty-eight.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I have taken up evening walks. I hope the weight is satisfactory.
[SEG0008] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature thirty-six point six. Oxygen ninety-eight percent. Respirations sixteen a minute. Please sit, he is coming.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. What is the problem.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, every spring I start sneezing, the eyes itch, and the nose runs. That is why I have come today.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Since, umm, well, from about...
[SEG0013] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): College onwards. Err, I am her sister. I came with her.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, thank you. Roughly eight years. Only in the spring, March to May.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): This year. Start date.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): The itching itself is worse than the sneezing, if I may say so.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): The date.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. Early March, but I cannot pin the day. It simply crept in.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Antihistamine.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I take cetrizine, but only sometimes, when a sneezing bout is too much.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Strength.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): The ten milligram tablet. My previous doctor had told me daily through the season, but I do not...
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She forgets. Half the strip is still in the drawer.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): That is correct, I am sorry. I skip many days.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Wheeze. Tightness.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No wheeze, doctor. No tightness in the chest.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Headache. Fever.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. And no, I do not get a headache.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nose blocked.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It runs only. It does not block.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Work.
[SEG0032] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tell him how you are by evening. She is finished.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): By four o'clock I feel like a wet rag, doctor. Utterly drained.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Where do you work.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): An open office. The air conditioning roars so much I can't hear myself think. That is the noise only, not an illness.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Throat.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): In the mornings there is a frog in my throat. I clear it often. A cup of tea settles it.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Eyes. Itch, watering, pain.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Itching, and they water, both eyes. As though chilli has been rubbed in. No pain, doctor.
[SEG0040] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She mouth-breathes after ten. You said the nose is not blocked, but it is.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I must correct myself. I denied it too quickly. At night the nose does get blocked, and I breathe through the mouth.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Short of breath.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I am not short of breath.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Drug allergies.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): None. Cetrizine has never caused a reaction.
[SEG0046] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I am allergic to house dust, doctor. Strongly. Same sneezing and itchy eyes.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Noted. That is your history, not hers. Let me look.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Conjunctivae mildly red. No discharge. Nasal lining pale and swollen. Chest clear, no wheeze.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Seasonal allergic rhinitis. Working impression. Not asthma.

[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stop the cetrizine today. Fexofenadine one hundred and eighty milligrams, one tablet by mouth every morning for the season. Olopatadine drops, zero point one percent, one drop in each eye twice a day for four weeks.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I will stop the cetrizine from today. Kindly, when should I return?

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): In four weeks. Keep the windows shut early morning, shower after you come indoors, and use a saline rinse at night if the nose blocks. If you start wheezing, come straight back.

spec.situation: Sneezing, itchy eyes and runny nose every spring; takes cetirizine 'sometimes'; sister is allergic to dust; no wheeze; doctor changes antihistamine and adds eye drops.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

omissions.text: This year's symptoms started in early March / symptoms occur specifically from March to May.
Patient stated the eye itching is worse than the sneezing.
Initial denial of nasal blockage was corrected: patient later said the nose gets blocked at night and she mouth-breathes after 10 pm.
Drug allergy history was specifically negative for drug allergies; patient said cetirizine has never caused a reaction.
Chest exam finding of 'chest clear' is not recorded, only absence of wheeze.
Doctor explicitly stated 'Not asthma' as part of the assessment.
